sections.content: Estar describes a temporary physical or emotional state, while sentirse focuses on how someone experiences that state. Spanish commonly combines sentirse with an adjective or other expression of condition. The distinction matters when describing symptoms, mood and changes in wellbeing.

items.spanish: Hoy estoy cansado, aunque ayer me sentía mejor.
items.english: Today I am tired, although yesterday I felt better.

items.spanish: Me siento mareado desde esta mañana.
items.english: I have felt dizzy since this morning.

items.spanish: Cuando estoy nerviosa, me cuesta dormir.
items.english: When I am nervous, I find it difficult to sleep.

items.spanish: Después de descansar, se sintió mucho más tranquilo.
items.english: After resting, he felt much calmer.

sections.content: Use estar to state a current condition and sentirse to focus on someone's subjective experience of that condition. Both can be followed by adjectives.
